pap.date: 8 Jan 2026 closes (PAP/Bloomberg table published 2026-01-09 07:04 (edition carries no row stamps; non-live rows taken as 8 Jan closes); US = US Treasury 8 Jan 2026 curve; live US/Japan quotes excluded)

policy.pricing_text: FRAs at the 8 Jan close (1x4 3.80, 3x6 3.58, 6x9 3.40, 9x12 3.37 vs WIBOR 3M 3.94) price roughly 55bp of NBP cuts within 12 months. The NBP survey of professional forecasters (2 Jan) sees an average reference rate of 3.69% in 2026. PKO (7 Jan): derivatives price a 3.25% reference rate by mid-2026; Deutsche Bank Polska (7 Jan) expects a January hold with core CPI at ~2.8%. MPC member Dąbrowski (Bloomberg, 8 Jan): a 50% chance of a January cut after the low December CPI, though he leans to a pause, and room for another 50bp by mid-2026; Tyrowicz (8 Jan): CPI may stay near target for the first time in this episode.
policy.risk_text: The January decision is a coin-toss for some members (Dąbrowski, 8 Jan) while most economists expect a hold: a hold would lift short FRAs/IRS a few bp (Millennium, 12-13 Jan), a cut would extend the front-end rally (PKO). If cuts are pushed beyond March, front-end roll-down does not materialise; heavy Q1 supply can widen asset swaps (Millennium, 9 Jan).

macro.projection_text: NBP November 2025 projection: CPI 3.7% (2025), 2.9% (2026), 2.5% (2027); December 2025 flash CPI 2.4% y/y.
macro.fiscal_text: 2025 general-government deficit ~6.9% of GDP (MoF plan); 2026 budget deficit cap PLN 271.7bn, gross borrowing needs ~PLN 690bn; Santander (19 Dec) noted the 10Y ASW back near 100bp on global fiscal worries.
macro.fiscal_risk_text: Q1 2026 supply of PLN 75-100bn over 8 auctions; Fitch (27 Feb) and Moody's (20 Mar) reviews with negative outlooks.
macro.backdrop_text: The NBP cut six times in 2025 to 4.00% (last on 3 Dec); CPI fell to 2.4% in December (flash, 31 Dec; final on 15 Jan, core estimated ~2.8% by Erste), the NBP projects 2.9% for 2026 (professional forecasters, 2 Jan: 2.6%). Manufacturing PMI fell to 48.5 in December (2 Jan). GDP grew 3.8% y/y in Q3. Ratings: Fitch A- negative, Moody's A2 negative, S&P A- stable. 8 Jan: MPC member Dąbrowski put a January cut at 50%; MoF priced EUR 3.25bn (5Y 2.964%, MS+43; 10Y 3.739%, MS+83; books over EUR 12bn); swaps rose 3-5bp (Millennium). Poland's December ESI rose to 100.0 but consumer inflation expectations jumped (35.3 from 27.9). Abroad: German factory orders +5.6% m/m (8 Jan), Brent +3.4% to $62 on supply worries; the US $200bn MBS purchase order came late on 8 Jan; US December payrolls are due on 9 Jan. Street views (December): PKO 1Q26 forecast 2Y 3.75 / 5Y 4.50 / 10Y 5.10 (reached by 7 Jan, PKO); Santander expects higher yields in Q1 on supply and cut repricing; ING says early-2026 trading follows MoF's Q1 issuance.

calendar.plan_text: MoF Q1 2026 financing plan (31 Dec 2025): 8 sale auctions for PLN 75-100bn, one switch auction, possible foreign issuance. January: sale auctions on 9 Jan (PLN 7-12bn), 22 Jan (8-13bn) and 28 Jan (7-12bn); no switch auction in January; 36-week T-bill auction on 16 Jan (PLN 2-4bn). 2026 gross borrowing needs ~PLN 690bn. BGK: FPC to issue domestically in 2026 (up to PLN 18.5bn). 9 Jan offer (MoF, 7 Jan): PLN 8-12bn in OK0128, PS0130, WZ0930, PS0131, NZ0331 (new 5Y compounded-POLSTR floater, 25 Mar 2031), DS1033 and DS1035. MoF priced EUR 3.25bn on 8 Jan (EUR 2bn Jan-2031 at 2.964%, MS+43; EUR 1.25bn Jun-2036 at 3.739%, MS+83). BGK announced an FPC auction for 12 Jan (FPC0229, FPC0231, FPC0332, FPC0235; min PLN 1.0bn).
calendar.timing_text: Within each auction week of the Aug 2025-Jan 2026 sample, yields drifted lower into the auction (rally regime) and the auction-day close was the cheapest point relative to the preceding session, so new buying is best executed at the auction-day close (9, 22, 28 Jan) rather than the day before. January supply is front-loaded (PLN 22-37bn across three auctions) after only ~21-23% pre-financing. For the front end the 13-14 Jan MPC is the event: a hold is the consensus, but Dąbrowski's 50% (8 Jan) means a cut is partly priced; the December final CPI (15 Jan) and the March projection drive the timing.

facts.core_text: Regime: the NBP paused at 4.00% with ~55bp more priced, the ECB is done at 2.00%, the Fed and BoE are easing gradually, the CNB and MNB are on hold. Poland's 5Y CDS was 59bp and the 10Y spread to Bunds 233bp on benchmark bonds (Erste, 8 Jan close; ~10bp less here on DS1035 vs the Bundesbank fitted 10Y). Poland priced EUR 3.25bn on 8 Jan at MS+43/+83bp: in EUR the curve trades well inside the PLN asset-swap levels.

quasi_takeaways: FPC fixed lines trade ~{lo}-{hi}bp over the POLGB curve (average {avg}bp); widest ASW {widest} at {widest_asw}bp. Same State Treasury guarantee as POLGBs.
Best pickup: {best} ({best_sp}bp vs POLGB). For buy-and-hold books the guarantee makes the pickup attractive; liquidity is the cost (Pekao became BGK market maker on 13 Nov 2025).

Supply: BGK announced an FPC auction for 12 Jan (FPC0229, FPC0231, FPC0332, FPC0235; minimum PLN 1.0bn, 8 Jan), the first of 2026 under a plan of up to PLN 18.5bn (24 Sep 2025). Expect secondary prints to cheapen into the auction; buy there rather than on Catalyst.
Use auctions, not Catalyst: trades are small retail lots and some lines go weeks without a print.
